sentences.text: Revenue, net interest plus noninterest income, compounded at 7.3% from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, while net income compounded at 9.7% [D5][D206][F113].
Revenue rose 22.9% in FY2023 on net interest income up 33.8%, which the filings tie to higher rates at the Corporate segment [D179][D174][P36].
Net income fell 20.0% in FY2020 then rose 65.8% in FY2021, while provisions swung from $17.5 billion to a $9.26 billion release [D94][D118][X142][X143].
The filings cited do not explain that swing, and FY2021 net income comes from the proxy statement, rounded [F26].
Revenue growth slowed to 2.8% in FY2025, with net interest income up 3.1% to $95.4 billion and noninterest income up 2.4% to $87.0 billion [D226][D221][F10][D222][F20].
The filing attributes net interest income growth to higher Markets income, Card revolving balances and wholesale deposits, largely offset by deposit margin compression [P28][D221].
Commercial and Investment Bank noninterest income rose 11.4% to $53.8 billion, while Asset and Wealth Management's rose 14.8% to $17.2 billion [S133][S134][S151][S152].
Operating leverage was negative: noninterest expense grew 4.2% against revenue growth of 2.8% [D225][D226].
Net income fell 2.6% on proxy-sourced figures, yet diluted EPS rose 1.4% as diluted shares fell 3.4% [D214][D216][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, against a window median of 57.2%, a low of 51.7% in FY2024 and a high of 59.2% in FY2022 [D207][D333][D331][D332].
Provision for credit losses rose to $14.2 billion, 7.8% of revenue against 6.0% in FY2024, a 1.8pp increase [X147][D208][D185].
The filing attributes $2.2 billion of a $3.2 billion allowance addition to the Apple Card transaction [P18][X147].
The largest move came in FY2023, when the ratio fell 4.1pp to 55.1% from 59.2%, as revenue grew 22.9% and expenses 14.5% [D160][D135][D179][D178].
The filing cites higher compensation and a $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment for the expense increase [P42][D178].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was an outflow of $148 billion in FY2025 [F60].
The filing attributes the outflow to higher trading assets, securities borrowed and held-for-sale loan originations [P21][F60].
Capital return is the better gauge: buybacks plus dividends were $48.2 billion, 84.5% of net income of $57.0 billion, against 57.5% in FY2024 [D205][X20][D182][X19].
Return on average equity was 16.1% against a peer median of 11.8%, ranking at the 100th percentile among seven banks [D213][D339][D338].
Cash and equivalents fell 26.8% to $343 billion, which the filing ties to Markets activities, higher securities, loans and Treasury and CIO deployment [D219][F100][P24].
Loans reached 57.3% of deposits from 55.0% a year earlier, as wholesale loans grew $121.1 billion on client demand [D211][D188][P4].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion accompanied a 3.4% fall in diluted shares to 2,781.5 million [X102][X112][D224][X92].
Credit costs: provisions reached 7.8% of revenue, the highest since FY2020's 14.6% and above the 6.0% peer median (n=4) [D208][D88][D341].
Credit quality: criticized exposure rose to $48.5 billion from $44.7 billion on downgrades, and nonaccrual loans rose $273 million [P2][P1].
Underlying interest income is stalling: net interest income excluding Markets was $92.6 billion, flat on the prior year [P28].
Data quality: FY2021 to FY2025 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K by up to 0.10%, and FY2020 pretax income and tax were recast [R1][F30][X20][R2][R3].
Efficiency ratio: a reading above 52.4% in the FY2026 10-K would reverse the cost-discipline trend, while one at or below the 51.7% window low would confirm it [D207][D331].
Provision share of revenue: a figure above 7.8% would confirm rising credit costs, while one below the 6.0% peer median would reverse them, in the FY2026 10-K [D208][D341].
Net interest income excluding Markets: a figure above $92.6 billion in the FY2026 10-K would show underlying growth resuming, while flat or lower would confirm the stall [P28].
